questions.question: Your uncle is a renowned scientist. He has neither contested nor won any election to the Rajya Sabha but he has recently become a member of the Rajya Sabha and has been appointed as a minister. How is this possible?

options.a: He was appointed by the Chief Justice of India
options.b: He was nominated by the President
options.c: He was appointed by the Prime Minister
options.d: He was nominated by the Governor

questions.solution: (b) He was nominated by the President. The President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha who have special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service; a nominated member can be made a minister.

questions.question: The house is discussing an issue regarding the nation in the month of November – December. Which session is in motion?
questions.solution: (b) Winter Session. Parliament's winter session is held in November–December (Budget: Feb–May; Monsoon: July–September).

questions.question: Which of the following is an Executive power of the President?
questions.solution: (a) Appointing the Prime Minister. Assent to bills, issuing ordinances and sending messages to Parliament are legislative powers.

questions.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question:
Choose the correct option to replace the underlined word.
Under Article 75 (3) of the Constitution, the Council of Ministers shall be collectively responsible to the [Prime Minister] (underlined).
questions.solution: (b) Lok Sabha. Under Article 75(3) the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: The Supreme Court has the power to review laws passed by the Union and State legislatures and if it is against the Constitution the Supreme Court can declare it null and void. This is referred to as the power of ______.
questions.solution: (c) Judicial Review: the power to declare laws/executive orders that violate the Constitution ultra vires, null and void.

questions.topic: Age limit of High Court judges
concepts: Age limit of High Court judges
questions.question: The maximum age in order to be qualified for appointment as a judge in the High Court is ______.
questions.solution: (a) 62 years. A High Court judge holds office till 62 years of age, so a person cannot be appointed beyond that age.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
Complete the analogy –
Early Nationalists were inspired by : the ideas of Western Philosophers
Assertive Nationalists were inspired by : ______
questions.solution: (c) India's Past. The Assertive Nationalists drew inspiration from India's glorious past and heritage (Shivaji, Ganapati festivals, Vedic culture), unlike the Early Nationalists who looked to Western liberal thinkers.

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the Muslim League –

options.a: to promote support for the British Government
options.b: to protect and advance the political rights of the Muslims
options.c: to promote hostility between Indian Muslims and other communities
options.d: to represent their needs to the government in mild and moderate language

questions.solution: (c) to promote hostility between Indian Muslims and other communities. The League's stated aim was to PREVENT any feeling of hostility among Muslims towards other communities.

questions.question: The Central Government of a country has decided to enforce a law that involves issuing licences to keep arms. Who among the following British Governor Generals had passed a similar law in India in 1878?
questions.solution: (a) Lord Lytton. His Arms Act of 1878 made it a criminal offence for Indians to carry arms without a licence (Europeans exempted).

questions.question: Who gave the slogan? ---- "Give me blood, I will give you freedom"
questions.solution: (d) Subhash Chandra Bose, while leading the Indian National Army.

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
questions.question:
Assertion : Gandhiji decided to launch a movement calling upon the British to Quit India immediately.
Reason : In 1942 Gandhiji declared that the presence of British in India was an invitation to Japan to invade India.

options.b: A is true but R is false
options.c: R is the correct explanation for A
options.d: A and R are independent of each other

questions.solution: (c) R is the correct explanation for A. With Japan advancing towards India's borders, Gandhiji held that the British presence was an invitation to Japan; hence the demand that the British quit India at once.

questions.question:
Which of the following are NOT the objectives of INA?
i. To organize an armed revolution and to fight the British army with modern arms.
ii. Introduction of new monetary and credit system.
iii. Total mobilisation of man power and money for total war.
iv. Abolition of Zamindari system.
questions.solution: (c) ii, iv. A new monetary and credit system and abolition of zamindari were objectives of the Forward Bloc; armed revolution and total mobilisation of men and money were INA objectives.

questions.question: Britain and France followed the policy of appeasement towards ______
questions.solution: (b) Germany and Italy. Britain and France appeased Hitler and Mussolini (e.g. Munich Pact 1938, Abyssinia).

questions.question:
Arrange the following events in Chronological order –
i) End of World War II
ii) Mountbatten Plan
iii) Cabinet Mission Plan
iv) Treaty of Versailles
questions.solution: (d) iv, i, iii, ii: Treaty of Versailles (1919), End of World War II (1945), Cabinet Mission Plan (1946), Mountbatten Plan (June 1947).

questions.question: Which Principal Organ is the Executive body of the United Nations Organisation?
questions.solution: (a) The Security Council, which is the executive body of the UN responsible for maintaining international peace and security.

questions.question: Who among the following is NOT considered as one of the founding fathers of Non Aligned Movement?
questions.solution: (d) Rajendra Prasad. The founders of NAM were Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno and Nkrumah.

questions.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question: State any two Administrative Powers of the Cabinet.
questions.solution: Any two: (1) The Cabinet formulates the policies of the government (internal and external) and ensures their implementation through the ministries. (2) It co-ordinates the working of the various ministries/departments. (3) It makes all important appointments (Governors, ambassadors, judges, Chiefs of the armed forces etc.), which the President makes on its advice. (4) It controls the administration, maintenance of law and order and the conduct of foreign relations.

marking_points.point: First administrative power of the Cabinet
Second administrative power of the Cabinet

questions.question: Briefly describe Appointment of the judges of the High Court.
questions.solution: The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President in consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the State. Other judges are appointed by the President in consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the State and the Chief Justice of that High Court (in practice on the recommendation of the Supreme Court collegium).

marking_points.point: Chief Justice appointed by the President after consulting the CJI and the Governor
Other judges appointed by the President after consulting the CJI, Governor and Chief Justice of the High Court

questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question: Name the trio in the given picture.
questions.solution: The trio is Lal-Bal-Pal: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal, the leading Assertive (Radical) Nationalists.

marking_points.point: Identifies the trio as Lal-Bal-Pal / names any two of them
Names all three: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal

questions.figure_desc: Photograph of three seated leaders (Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal).

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
questions.question: What did the Rowlatt Act imply? (any four points)
questions.solution: The Rowlatt Act (March 1919) implied: (1) any person could be arrested on mere suspicion without a warrant; (2) a person could be detained/imprisoned without trial; (3) trials could be held in camera by special courts with no right of appeal; (4) the accused had no right to know the name of the accuser or the evidence against him; (5) press freedom was curbed. It was called the 'Black Act' — 'no dalil, no vakil, no appeal'.

marking_points.point: Any two of the four implications (arrest without warrant / detention without trial)
Any other two implications (no appeal, secret trial, accuser not named, press curbed)

questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
questions.question:
[Picture: protesters holding a banner 'SIMON GO BACK!']
Identify the movement associated with the above slogan. Why did the Indian leaders decide to boycott it?
questions.solution: The slogan 'Simon Go Back' is associated with the protest/boycott of the Simon Commission (1928). Indian leaders boycotted it because it was an all-white commission with no Indian member, although it was to decide India's constitutional future — an insult to Indian self-respect.

marking_points.point: Identifies the boycott of the Simon Commission (1928)
Reason: all-white commission with no Indian member

questions.question: Describe Role of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru in the Non Aligned Movement.
questions.solution: Nehru was one of the founders and chief architects of NAM. He rejected joining either the US or Soviet bloc, advocated an independent foreign policy based on Panchsheel and peaceful co-existence, took a lead role at the Bandung Conference (1955) and the Belgrade Summit (1961), opposed colonialism and racialism, and worked for disarmament and world peace.

marking_points.point: Founder/architect of NAM; kept India away from power blocs
Panchsheel/peaceful co-existence, Bandung & Belgrade, anti-colonialism or disarmament

questions.question: Name the two journals published by the World Health Organisation to create health consciousness among people.
questions.solution: The WHO publishes the journals 'World Health' and 'WHO Chronicle' (accept also 'International Digest of Health Legislation' / 'Bulletin of the WHO').

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.topic: Rajya Sabha Chairman and exclusive powers
concepts: Rajya Sabha Chairman and exclusive powers
questions.question:
With reference to the Union Parliament, answer the following questions:
"Rajya Sabha adjourned till December 16 amid ruckus over no-trust motion against chairman. Opposition parties, led by the Congress, have submitted a notice to move a motion to remove Dhankhar, accusing him of being 'extremely partisan'." (Source: The Hindu, Updated December 13, 2024, New Delhi)
(a) Who can adjourn the above house? Write any two exclusive powers of this house.
questions.solution: The Rajya Sabha can be adjourned by its Chairman — the Vice-President of India (at the time, Jagdeep Dhankhar). Exclusive powers (any two): (1) Under Art. 249 it can, by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, declare a subject in the State List to be of national importance, enabling Parliament to legislate on it. (2) Under Art. 312 it can, by a two-thirds majority, authorise Parliament to create new All-India Services. (3) A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can be initiated only in the Rajya Sabha.

marking_points.point: Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) adjourns the House

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
With reference to the Union Parliament, answer the following questions:
"Rajya Sabha adjourned till December 16 amid ruckus over no-trust motion against chairman. Opposition parties, led by the Congress, have submitted a notice to move a motion to remove Dhankhar, accusing him of being 'extremely partisan'." (Source: The Hindu, Updated December 13, 2024, New Delhi)
(b) Who is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha? Write any two of his disciplinary functions.
questions.solution: The Speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha. Disciplinary functions (any two): (1) maintains order and decorum in the House; (2) can warn, name or ask a member guilty of disorderly conduct to withdraw, and can suspend a member; (3) can adjourn or suspend the sitting in case of grave disorder; (4) decides points of order and can expunge unparliamentary remarks; (5) decides on disqualification of members on grounds of defection.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
With reference to the Union Parliament, answer the following questions:
"Rajya Sabha adjourned till December 16 amid ruckus over no-trust motion against chairman. Opposition parties, led by the Congress, have submitted a notice to move a motion to remove Dhankhar, accusing him of being 'extremely partisan'." (Source: The Hindu, Updated December 13, 2024, New Delhi)
(c) State any four Legislative Powers of the Parliament.
questions.solution: Any four: (1) Parliament makes laws on all subjects of the Union List. (2) It shares power with State legislatures on the Concurrent List; in case of conflict the Union law prevails. (3) It has residuary powers to legislate on subjects not in any list. (4) It can legislate on State List subjects if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution under Art. 249, during a National Emergency, or when two or more states request it. (5) It can make laws for a state under President's Rule. (6) Ordinances issued by the President must be approved by Parliament within six weeks of its reassembly. (7) It can amend the Constitution.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
With reference to the Union Executive, answer the following questions:
[Picture: a lady seated beside the Indian national flag]
(a) Identify the above personality. Mention any two points to enumerate the Financial Powers vested in the above executive head.
questions.solution: The personality is Smt. Droupadi Murmu, the President of India. Financial powers (any two): (1) Money Bills can be introduced in the Lok Sabha only with the prior recommendation of the President. (2) The annual budget (Annual Financial Statement) is laid before Parliament on her behalf. (3) No demand for grant can be made except on her recommendation. (4) The Contingency Fund of India is at her disposal to meet unforeseen expenditure. (5) She appoints the Finance Commission every five years.

marking_points.point: Identifies Droupadi Murmu, President of India

questions.figure_desc: Photograph of President Droupadi Murmu seated beside the Indian national flag.

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question:
With reference to the Union Executive, answer the following questions:
(b) While the President of India is the nominal head of the State, the Prime Minister is the real head of the Nation. Write the position and power of the Prime Minister in relation with the President.
questions.solution: The PM is the link/channel of communication between the President and the Council of Ministers (Art. 78): (1) the PM communicates to the President all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to administration and proposals for legislation; (2) furnishes information the President calls for and, if the President so requires, submits for the Council's consideration any matter decided by a single minister; (3) the President makes all important appointments (ministers, Governors, ambassadors, judges, Attorney General etc.) on the advice of the PM; (4) the PM advises the President on summoning and proroguing Parliament and dissolution of the Lok Sabha. The President is bound to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the PM (Art. 74).

marking_points.point: PM as link between President and Council of Ministers / communicates decisions
Appointments made by the President on PM's advice
Advises on summoning/prorogation/dissolution or binding advice under Art. 74

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.chapter: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
questions.question:
With reference to the Union Executive, answer the following questions:
(c) Write any four points of differences between the Council of Ministers and the Cabinet.
questions.solution: (1) Size: the Council of Ministers is a large body (about 60-70; max 15% of Lok Sabha strength) including Cabinet ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers; the Cabinet is a small body of 15-20 senior ministers. (2) Meetings: the Council rarely meets as a whole; the Cabinet meets frequently (usually weekly). (3) Functions: the Cabinet formulates policies and takes all important decisions; the Council of Ministers implements the decisions of the Cabinet. (4) Constitutional status: the Council of Ministers is mentioned in the original Constitution (Art. 74, 75); the Cabinet was added only by the 44th Amendment (1978) in Art. 352. (5) Collective responsibility is to the Lok Sabha for the Council, but decisions binding on it are taken by the Cabinet.

marking_points.point: Difference in constitutional status or any other valid difference

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
With reference to the Indian Judiciary, answer the following questions:
(a) Mention any three ways in which the Constitution ensures the independence of judiciary from the control of Executive and Legislature.
questions.solution: Any three: (1) Judges are appointed by the President in consultation with the CJI/collegium, not by political choice. (2) Security of tenure: they hold office till 65 (SC)/62 (HC) and can be removed only by impeachment on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. (3) Salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, not voted by Parliament, and cannot be reduced during their term (except during a Financial Emergency). (4) The conduct of judges cannot be discussed in Parliament except during an impeachment motion. (5) Retired SC judges cannot practise in any court in India. (6) The Supreme Court can punish for contempt of court. (7) Separation of the judiciary from the executive (Art. 50).

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
With reference to the Indian Judiciary, answer the following questions:
(b) Supreme Court of India is called as a Court of Record. Justify this statement with any three points.
questions.solution: (1) The judgments and proceedings of the Supreme Court are recorded and preserved for perpetual memory and testimony. (2) These records serve as precedents and are binding on all lower courts and are admissible as evidence; they cannot be questioned in any court. (3) As a Court of Record, the Supreme Court has the power to punish for contempt of itself (Art. 129).

marking_points.point: Records act as binding precedents/evidence for lower courts
Power to punish for contempt of court

questions.choice_note: any 2 of 3 questions in Section A
questions.question:
With reference to the Indian Judiciary, answer the following questions:
(c) What are Lok Adalats also known as? Write any three advantages of the Lok Adalats.
questions.solution: Lok Adalats are also known as 'People's Courts'. Advantages (any three): (1) speedy justice — cases settled quickly by mutual compromise; (2) economical — no court fee, and fee paid is refunded if settled; (3) reduce the burden/backlog of regular courts; (4) informal procedure; parties can talk directly; (5) the award is final and binding with no appeal, ending litigation; (6) especially helpful to the poor and weaker sections.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the First War of Independence, 1857 and Growth of Nationalism answer the following questions:
(a) Describe Disrespect shown to Bahadur Shah Zafar as the cause for the rise of the First War of Indian Independence, 1857.
questions.solution: (1) Lord Dalhousie announced that Bahadur Shah Zafar's successors would not be allowed to use the imperial title or to live in the Red Fort, and would have to shift to Qutub/Mehrauli. (2) Lord Canning further announced that after Bahadur Shah's death his successors would lose the title of 'King' and be called mere 'Princes'. (3) The Company stopped presenting nazars to the Mughal emperor and removed his name from coins. These insults to the symbol of Mughal authority hurt the sentiments of Indians, especially Muslims, and caused resentment that fed the revolt.

marking_points.point: Dalhousie: successors to leave the Red Fort / lose imperial title
Canning: successors to be called only 'Princes' / name removed from coins
This hurt Indian (esp. Muslim) sentiments and fuelled the revolt

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the First War of Independence, 1857 and Growth of Nationalism answer the following questions:
(b) Repressive policies of Lord Lytton acted as a catalyst for the growth of nationalist movement in India. Describe any three such policies of Lord Lytton.
questions.solution: Any three: (1) Vernacular Press Act, 1878 — imposed severe restrictions on newspapers in Indian languages, while English papers were exempt. (2) Arms Act, 1878 — made it a criminal offence for Indians to carry arms without a licence; Europeans and Anglo-Indians were exempt. (3) Grand Delhi Durbar, 1877 — held at huge expense to proclaim Queen Victoria Empress of India while millions were dying in famine. (4) Reduction of the maximum age for the ICS exam from 21 to 19, making it harder for Indians to compete. (5) Removal of import duties on British cotton goods, harming Indian textile industry.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.topic: First session of INC and aims
concepts: First session of INC and aims
questions.question:
With reference to the First War of Independence, 1857 and Growth of Nationalism answer the following questions:
(c) Under whose Presidentship was the First Session of the Congress held? Write any three aims of the Indian National Congress.
questions.solution: The first session (Bombay, December 1885) was presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee). Aims (any three): (1) to promote friendly relations among nationalist political workers from different parts of the country; (2) to develop and consolidate feelings of national unity irrespective of caste, religion or province; (3) to formulate popular demands and present them to the government; (4) to train and organise public opinion in the country; (5) to remove racial, religious and provincial prejudices.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: First Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
With reference to the First and the Second Phase of Indian National Movement and the Muslim League answer the following questions:
(a) What was Dadabhai Naoroji popularly known as? Name the newspaper edited by him and the magazine started by him.
questions.solution: Dadabhai Naoroji was popularly known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'. He edited the newspaper 'Rast Goftar' and started the magazine 'Voice of India'.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
With reference to the First and the Second Phase of Indian National Movement and the Muslim League answer the following questions:
[Picture: portrait of a leader wearing a turban and shawl]
(b) Identify the above personality. Write any two of his contributions in the Indian Freedom Struggle movement.
questions.solution: The personality is Bal Gangadhar Tilak ('Lokmanya'). Contributions (any two): (1) declared 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'; (2) through his newspapers Kesari (Marathi) and Maratha (English) he criticised British policies and aroused national consciousness; (3) organised Ganapati (1893) and Shivaji (1895) festivals to spread nationalism among the masses; (4) promoted Swadeshi, boycott and national education (Deccan Education Society); (5) founded the Home Rule League (1916) and worked for the Lucknow Pact.
questions.figure_desc: Portrait photograph of a moustached leader in a Puneri turban and shawl (Bal Gangadhar Tilak).

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Second Phase of Indian National Movement
questions.question:
With reference to the First and the Second Phase of Indian National Movement and the Muslim League answer the following questions:
(c) A joint scheme of political reforms was put forward and adopted by the Congress and the Muslim League in 1916 known as the Lucknow Pact. Mention the Significance of the Lucknow Pact.
questions.solution: Significance: (1) it reunited the Moderates and the Extremists in the Congress; (2) it brought the Congress and the Muslim League together on a common platform with joint demands (self-government, Indian majority in councils), showing Hindu-Muslim unity; (3) the joint demands put greater pressure on the British, leading to the August Declaration of 1917 promising responsible government; (4) however, by accepting separate electorates for Muslims, the Congress gave legitimacy to communal representation, which later strengthened communal politics.

marking_points.point: Joint demands pressured the British (August Declaration 1917)
Acceptance of separate electorates — sowed seeds of communal politics

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.chapter: Gandhian Era and Struggle for Independence
questions.question:
With reference to Mahatama Gandhi and the National movement and Independence and Partition of India answer the following questions:
[Picture: a tall memorial structure with a sculpture garden]
(a) Identify the above structure. Where is it located? Which movement started by Gandhi ji is associated with this memorial? State any two impacts of this movement.
questions.solution: It is the National Salt Satyagraha Memorial at Dandi (Navsari district, Gujarat). It is associated with the Civil Disobedience Movement, launched with the Dandi March/Salt Satyagraha (12 March–6 April 1930). Impacts (any two): (1) it became a mass movement drawing women, peasants, students and businessmen in large numbers; (2) people broke salt laws, boycotted foreign goods and refused taxes, causing a fall in British imports; (3) it spread to all parts of the country (e.g. Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan in NWFP) and won worldwide attention; (4) the British were forced to negotiate — Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) and Round Table Conference.

marking_points.point: Identifies National Salt Satyagraha Memorial, Dandi, Gujarat

questions.figure_desc: Photograph of the tall National Salt Satyagraha Memorial at Dandi with surrounding statues.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to Mahatama Gandhi and the National movement and Independence and Partition of India answer the following questions:
(b) Write the Objectives of the Forward Bloc which was formed on May 3, 1939.
questions.solution: Objectives of the Forward Bloc (any three): (1) to rally all radical and leftist elements and fight imperialism uncompromisingly for complete independence; (2) abolition of landlordism/zamindari system; (3) a new monetary and credit system; (4) industrialisation and modernisation of agriculture on socialist lines; (5) a socialist reorganisation of society with equality and an end to exploitation.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Constituent Assembly composition; Mountbatten Plan on NWFP
concepts: Constituent Assembly composition; Mountbatten Plan on NWFP
questions.question:
With reference to Mahatama Gandhi and the National movement and Independence and Partition of India answer the following questions:
(c) Constituent Assembly would be set up to frame the new Constitution of India according to the Cabinet Mission Plan, write its composition. What did the Mountbatten Plan state about the North West Frontier Provinces?
questions.solution: Composition under the Cabinet Mission Plan: the Constituent Assembly was to have 389 members — 292 elected by the provincial legislative assemblies (roughly one member per ten lakh population, seats divided among General, Muslim and Sikh communities in proportion to population), 4 from Chief Commissioners' provinces and 93 representatives of the Princely States. Mountbatten Plan on NWFP: a referendum would be held in the North West Frontier Province to decide whether it would join India or Pakistan.

marking_points.point: 389 members; 292 from British provinces elected by provincial assemblies (one per ~10 lakh)
93 from Princely States + 4 Chief Commissioners' provinces; seats by community
To decide whether to join India or Pakistan

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the First and the Second World Wars and Rise of Dictatorships answer the following questions:
(a) Mention any three points to describe how Europe was reorganised (territorial rearrangement) after the First World War.
questions.solution: Any three: (1) Alsace-Lorraine was returned by Germany to France; the Saar coal mines given to France for 15 years. (2) New independent states were created — Poland, Czechoslovakia, Yugoslavia, Austria, Hungary; Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania became independent. (3) Poland was given the Polish Corridor to the sea; Danzig made a free city under the League. (4) Eupen and Malmedy went to Belgium; North Schleswig to Denmark; Memel to Lithuania. (5) The Austro-Hungarian empire was dismembered and Germany lost all her overseas colonies (as mandates under the League). (6) The Rhineland was demilitarised.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the First and the Second World Wars and Rise of Dictatorships answer the following questions:
(b) Describe Economic Crisis as a cause for the rise of Fascism in Italy.
questions.solution: After WWI Italy faced a severe economic crisis: (1) the war had cost huge sums; the country was burdened with debt and a heavy deficit; (2) industries closed after the war, causing massive unemployment, worsened by demobilised soldiers returning home; (3) there was acute shortage of food and rising prices/inflation; (4) widespread strikes, lockouts and peasant unrest followed, and the weak governments could not cope. The people turned to Mussolini's Fascist Party, which promised order, jobs and prosperity.

marking_points.point: Unemployment, inflation and shortage of food
Strikes and unrest; weak governments led people to support Mussolini

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Division of Germany; effect on Japan
concepts: Division of Germany; effect on Japan
questions.question:
With reference to the First and the Second World Wars and Rise of Dictatorships answer the following questions:
(c) At the end of Second World War Germany was divided into two zones, describe these two zones. Explain what was the effect of Second World War on Japan?
questions.solution: Division of Germany: Germany (and Berlin) was first divided into four occupation zones; the zones of the USA, Britain and France formed West Germany (Federal Republic of Germany, democratic, capitalist), while the Soviet zone became East Germany (German Democratic Republic, communist). Effect on Japan: (1) the atom bombs on Hiroshima (6 Aug 1945) and Nagasaki (9 Aug 1945) caused enormous destruction and Japan surrendered unconditionally; (2) Japan was occupied by Allied (American) forces under General MacArthur till 1952, lost the territories she had conquered, adopted a new democratic Constitution (1947) and renounced war.

marking_points.point: West Germany (FRG) — zones of USA, Britain and France
Atomic bombing and unconditional surrender of Japan
Allied/US occupation, loss of territory, new democratic constitution

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the Organs and Agencies of the United Nations Organisation answer the following questions:
[Picture: the Peace Palace building]
(a) Observe the above picture and name the Judicial organ of the United Nations Organisation. Write its composition.
questions.solution: The building is the Peace Palace at The Hague (Netherlands), seat of the International Court of Justice — the judicial organ of the UN. Composition: 15 judges elected by the General Assembly and the Security Council voting independently (absolute majority in both); no two judges from the same nation; term of 9 years, one-third retiring every 3 years; they are eligible for re-election; the judges elect a President and Vice-President for 3 years.

questions.question:
With reference to the Organs and Agencies of the United Nations Organisation answer the following questions:
(b) Describe any three functions of the General Assembly.
questions.solution: Any three: (1) Deliberative — discusses any matter within the scope of the Charter and makes recommendations for maintaining international peace and security. (2) Financial — considers and approves the UN budget and apportions expenses among members. (3) Elective — elects the non-permanent members of the Security Council, members of ECOSOC, and (with the SC) the judges of the ICJ; appoints the Secretary-General on SC recommendation. (4) Admits new members on SC recommendation and can suspend/expel members. (5) Amends the Charter; receives reports from other organs. (6) Under the Uniting for Peace Resolution (1950) can act if the SC fails due to veto.

questions.choice_note: any 3 of 5 questions in Section B
questions.question:
With reference to the Organs and Agencies of the United Nations Organisation answer the following questions:
(c) Write the expanded form of UNESCO. Mention three of its functions in the field of Preservation of Cultural Heritage.
questions.solution: UNESCO: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation. Functions for preserving cultural heritage (any three): (1) identifies and declares monuments and sites of outstanding value as World Heritage Sites and helps protect and restore them (e.g. Abu Simbel temples in Egypt, Mohenjo-daro); (2) gives financial and technical assistance to member nations for preserving monuments, manuscripts and works of art; (3) encourages the protection of intangible heritage — languages, folk arts, music and traditions; (4) promotes cultural exchange and understanding among nations; (5) works to prevent illicit trafficking of cultural property.

marking_points.point: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation
